title: One Wrong Stroke and the Whole Scroll Is Ruined | China Travel Expert
description:
In Chinese calligraphy, one wrong stroke can ruin the whole scroll — and there's no undo.

On raw xuan paper the ink soaks in the instant the brush touches down. If you try to fix or retrace a line, that spot dries darker than the original stroke — so it can never be touched up. That's why every stroke has to be one single, continuous movement. Xuan paper's thirst for ink is exactly what lets a master separate the lightest and heaviest strokes on the same character.

🧭 Expert Tip: Try a beginner brush class — most Chinese cities and old towns offer drop-in calligraphy sessions for travelers.
